title: decompose-presubmit-lint-into-language-aware-fanout-and-add-dep-metadata-index
author: Ava Morgan
commits: split(lint): introduce language plugin interface and JS/Python plugins
ci(presubmit): add presubmit fanout dispatcher and shard manifest
tooling(dep): add dep-metadata-index and indexing CLI
ci(workflows): convert presubmit workflow to fanout + lightweight runners
docs: presubmit developer guide and rollout checklist
description:
Motivation:
The monolithic presubmit lint runner is fragile and slow to evolve for language-specific rules. We want a maintainable path forward that: 1) allows per-language lint/test adapters, 2) reduces CI time by fanout + targeted shards, and 3) surfaces dependency metadata to make dep-updates and dep-bot decisions safer.

Summary of changes (single-pass description):
- Introduces a small presubmit dispatcher (ci/presubmit/dispatcher.py) that reads ci/presubmit/shards.yaml and fans a single GitHub workflow run into a set of targeted lightweight presubmit jobs. The dispatcher is intentionally side-effect-minimal and designed to run as a step in the existing presubmit workflow.
- Replaces the single monolithic lint step with a plugin interface (scripts/lint_plugins/__init__.py) and two initial language plugins (js_plugin.py, py_plugin.py). Each plugin is responsible for selecting files and invoking the existing lint/test tooling in a hermetic way.
- Adds tools/dep_index, a small dependency metadata indexer and lightweight CLI that produces a canonical JSON index used by depbots/integrations. The index captures package name, lockfile location, dependency type (direct/transitive), and last-updated hint. This reduces blind upgrades and makes rollback decisions deterministic.
- Updates .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to run an initial dispatcher step which then spawns language-specific job shards (via workflow_dispatch hooks). The workflow now uses smaller Docker images (docker/presubmit/Dockerfile.small) to reduce startup latency for these short-lived jobs.
- Adds ci/cache/priming.sh to warm common caches when a shard set is large; the dispatcher decides whether to prime caches based on changed file sizes and aggregate shard count.
- Small CI and developer-facing docs (docs/dev/presubmit-fanout.md) and an example shard config in examples/presubmit.

Implementation notes and rationale:
- Plugin interface: minimal, synchronous API (select_files(changed_paths) -> list_of_targets; run(targets) -> exit_code, output). This keeps language-specific logic decoupled from the dispatcher and avoids huge cross-language dependencies in the core CI runner.
- Presubmit shards manifest: ci/presubmit/shards.yaml is declarative and supports rules like: include when path matches, minimum job weight, and preferred runner label. This lets teams opt-in to language shards without repo-wide rewrites.
- Dep metadata index: the index is intentionally conservative (only metadata) so it's safe for on-prem/private deployments; no telemetry is sent by default. The indexer supports a --local-only flag for air-gapped installs.
- Backward compatibility: For repos that rely on the old monolith, the dispatcher includes a fallback mode (legacy_shard) that runs the previous runner if no plugins match. This was key to an incremental rollout.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for the dispatcher and adapters (pkg/ci/runner/*_test.go). Integration smoke runs executed in ephemeral runners to validate workflow dispatch and job creation.
- Added a small e2e harness in Makefile.ci that simulates a change set and validates expected shard creation.
- CI outcomes: the branch passed the full presubmit matrix after three reruns to warm caches. Final CI status: pass.

Review notes (conversation highlights captured here):
- Diego Rivera: "Nice separation. Two asks: 1) make shard weighting explicit in the manifest so we can tune cost vs latency per language; 2) add a short-circuit if no changed files match to avoid unnecessary workflow_dispatch spikes."
  - Author response (Ava): "Added weight and no-op early exit in shards.yaml and dispatcher; see commit 'ci: shard no-op guard'."
- Priya Shah: "Can dep-index run in the builder image and emit a deterministic artifact? We want reproducible indexes for CI audits."
  - Author response: "Indexer now has --stamp option to write a reproducible artifact and a small note in tools/dep_index/README.md describing how to reproduce."
- Connor Lee: "Small nit: Dockerfile.small should pin the base image digest to avoid flakiness in the short term."
  - Author response: "Pinned digest and added a CI gate to detect unexpected base-image changes."
- Marie Dubois: "Will this increase noise for small PRs? Fans of small PRs may suffer if we spawn too many runners."
  - Author response: "Dispatcher only creates shards that match changed files and will collapse to a single lightweight shard for tiny changes; added test coverage to validate collapse behavior."

Rollout plan and safety:
- Merged behind a feature flag (ci.presubmit.fanout.enabled) defaulting to off. We enabled for two teams and monitored presubmit cost and latency. After two weeks of stability, we enabled org-wide.
- If the dispatcher or any plugin fails, the dispatcher will fall back to legacy_shard mode and post a diagnostic comment on the PR with a YAML snippet for quick reproduction. This fallback path was tested during the staged rollout.

Observability and follow-ups:
- Added metrics emitted by the dispatcher: presubmit.shard.count, presubmit.shard.duration, presubmit.fallback.count. These integrate with existing presubmit dashboards.
- Follow-up work items: ENG-2101 (add Go plugin), ENG-2102 (presubmit cost exporter per-PR), ENG-2110 (make dep-index available to dep-bot for safe auto-upgrades).

Files changed (high-level):
- ci/presubmit/*: dispatcher, shard manifest, cache priming script.
- scripts/lint_plugins/*: plugin interface and initial language plugins.
- tools/dep_index/*: indexer, README, packaging.
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml: converted to dispatcher-first flow.
- docker/presubmit/Dockerfile.small: smaller runtime image for shards.

Merge notes:
- Addressed requested changes from reviewers; squashed commits and merged via squash merge on 2026-02-20. Post-merge: a small hotfix (PR 102338) fixed a race where the dispatcher attempted workflow_dispatch for already-closed PRs.

Impact:
- Median presubmit feedback time for non-monolithic changes dropped by ~28% in early rollout teams. CI cost per-PR dropped by ~14% due to smaller images and targeted shards. Dep upgrade rollover velocity improved with dep-index metadata available to the depbot integration.

If you need to revert: flip ci.presubmit.fanout.enabled=false in repo settings and revert the small dispatcher step in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml.
review_comments: Diego Rivera: Please make shard weighting explicit and add a no-op spike guard.
Priya Shah: Reproducible dep-index artifacts would be ideal for auditing.
Connor Lee: Pin Docker base digest to reduce image drift flakiness.
Marie Dubois: Ensure we don't spawn shards for tiny changes (noise concern).
release_notes: Introduce presubmit fanout dispatcher, language-aware lint plugins, and a dep-metadata indexer. Improves presubmit latency and reduces CI cost by targeting shards. Backwards compatible fallback included.
